title: Super Fantasy: Night of the Badly Dead - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xTpYdSgeWPc

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a quick look at Super Fantasy: Night of the Badly Dead and warns that its looks are deceptive. The standees are thin, the wooden tombstones plain, the equipment printed on odd cardboard chips, and the rulebook, probably translated from Italian, has spelling errors and ambiguities. You might walk past it at a convention as a kid's first crawl. That, he says, would be a mistake.

Underneath is a brutal, tactical co-op skirmish crawl across six escalating graveyard missions, each with an optional "epic" win. Each hero splits a pool of six custom d6 between moving, attacking, smashing tombstones, charging abilities and defending. Wilds count as the stat being tested, so Kayla Skullkicker's speed of two turns a star into two squares. Smashed tombstones cover enemy spawn points. A hero with zero armor is hit automatically, so whole turns go into banking shield tokens. Ranged weapons fire at exactly their listed distance. Enemies activate only in orthogonally adjacent areas, so where the party ends its turn decides who acts, and push effects can shove threats out of reach.

A dead hero costs a turn off the clock rather than the game. He finds three heroes the solo sweet spot, highly recommends it, and promises a separate look at the second volume.

----

Under kid-crawl looks, this one hides a punishing tactical engine. What's a game you nearly dismissed on looks alone?
